the pressure-induced structural changes in ZIF-7 are not only metal-dependent but also metal-specific, and that the structural change in ZIF-9 and CdIF-13 can be attributed to different mechanisms.
the step-shaped adsorption behavior in ZIFs is highly tunable, and the step positions can be controlled with metal substitution.

the step-shaped adsorption behavior observed in these flexible ZIfs can be tuned through chemical modification.

we have shown that metal substitution can be utilized to tune the pressure-responsive adsorption properties of flexible ZIFs, and that these materials are highly promising for high-capacity adsorption of CO2 and CH 4 at high pressures.

the metal substitution in ZIFs can be used to tune the adsorption properties of the framework, and thus the metal substitution can be used to tailor the properties of the ZIFs for a specific application.
The main takeaway from our work is that
metal substitution in flexible ZIFs can lead to dramatic changes in adsorption capacity, step position, and pre-step uptake, and that a single-crystal phase change can occur in Cd-containing ZIFs.
the metal center of flexible ZIFs has a profound influence on the pressure-induced phase changes, and thus on the resulting gas adsorption behavior and step positions.
the pressure-induced step-shaped adsorption behavior of ZIFs can be tuned by metal substitution, which provides a new avenue for the design of high-capacity, step-shaped adsorbents.
